title: Planning to Fairly Allocate: Probabilistic Fairness in the Restless Bandit Setting

problem.claim: Budget-constrained resource allocation with action-dependent arm transitions can be modeled using restless and collapsing bandits.

gap.claim: Existing Whittle-index-based approaches either do not consider fairness among arms or incentivize fairness without guaranteeing it.

contributions.claim: Introduces ProbFair, a policy that maximizes total expected reward, satisfies the budget constraint, and maintains a strictly positive lower bound on the probability of pulling each arm at every timestep.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The algorithm is evaluated on a real-world application involving interventions supporting CPAP therapy adherence among patients.
The algorithm is also evaluated on a broader class of synthetic transition matrices.
The authors report that ProbFair preserves utility while providing fairness guarantees.

narrative_sequence.summary: Restless and collapsing bandits model budget-constrained allocation with action-dependent transition probabilities.
Whittle-index-based approaches do not guarantee fairness or do not consider it.
ProbFair is introduced to optimize expected reward under the budget while enforcing a positive per-timestep pulling probability.
The method is evaluated in a CPAP adherence application and on synthetic transition matrices, with reported utility preservation and fairness guarantees.

source_observation.claim: A policy can combine utility maximization, budget feasibility, and a positive lower bound on selection probability.

interpretation.claim: Fairness can be encoded as a probabilistic service guarantee while retaining the primary allocation objective.

application.claim: Resource-allocation systems may use probabilistic lower bounds to prevent arms or recipients from being systematically neglected.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how the guarantee behaves under different budgets, transition structures, or operational constraints.

unknowns: The specific ProbFair algorithm and its optimization procedure are not described.
The numerical fairness bound and budget formulation are not provided.
The evaluation baselines, metrics, datasets, transition matrices, and quantitative results are not specified.
The scope and assumptions of the fairness guarantee are not stated.
